claims.text: The initial HEA multilayer interfaces are incoherent.
Diffusion-mediated creep predominates in the initial HEA multilayer at high temperature.
An ultrathin B2-ordered NiAl-type interlayer can be formed between the HEA layers.
A B2-ordered NiAl-type interlayer will increase interface coherency.
Incoherent interfaces permit rapid diffusion-controlled deformation at 900–1000 °C.
The B2-ordered interlayer bridges adjacent HEA layers coherently.
The B2-ordered interlayer reduces mismatch between adjacent HEA layers.
The ordered interlayer acts as a barrier to atomic diffusion.
The coherent B2 interlayer reduces fast-diffusion paths at the interface.
The coherent B2 interlayer improves stress transmission across the interface.
Reducing interfacial diffusion limits diffusion-assisted dislocation climb.
The interlayer shifts creep from diffusion-mediated deformation to deformation controlled by dislocation activity.
In the shifted regime, deformation is controlled by dislocation glide and climb within a coherent lattice.
Adding the B2 interlayer will increase the activation energy for creep.
Adding the B2 interlayer will reduce the steady-state creep rate.
The beneficial effect requires an interlayer thin enough to preserve multilayer cohesion.
The beneficial effect requires crystallographic alignment between the interlayer and HEA layers.
Excessive interlayer thickness or composition mismatch may negate the beneficial effect.

contradictions.description: The mechanism says suppression of diffusion limits dislocation climb, but then describes the resulting dislocation-mediated regime as controlled by both glide and climb. Because climb is itself generally diffusion-assisted, its proposed role in the shifted regime is internally ambiguous.
